localization.TOURS.NarratorsCallDescription: How rolls start at this table: the Narrator calls for one, and both sides finish it in the same window.
localization.TOURS.NarratorsCallIntroTitle: The Narrator calls for the roll
localization.TOURS.NarratorsCallIntroContent:
In Legend in the Mist the Narrator decides an action needs dice and picks how it resolves — a Quick outcome, a Detailed one, or a Reaction (Core Book p.269).

So rolls here start with you, not with a player pressing a button. This tour walks that path: calling for a roll, sharing the window, and Acting Together as a group.
localization.TOURS.NarratorsCallSidebarTitle: Call from where you already are
localization.TOURS.NarratorsCallSidebarContent: The Tags sidebar is your view of the whole scene, so the call lives here. One click and you are picking who rolls.
localization.TOURS.NarratorsCallPickWhoContent:
Each row names the Hero and the player holding them. If nobody is connected, the roll falls to you and you make it on their behalf.

Pick one and their Actions appear beside the roster — choosing an Action is optional, and it only fills in what the roll is for. Everything else — the move, the Might, the tags you invoke — you set inside the roll window itself, where the player can watch you do it.
localization.TOURS.NarratorsCallActingTogetherContent:
When the whole group pushes at the same thing, that is one roll, not several (Core Book p.157). The Fellowship is the last row of the roster, so calling on the group is the same gesture as calling on one Hero.

Every Hero in the Fellowship is in it — there is nobody to tick. The roll rides the Fellowship, you press the dice, and each Hero contributes a single tag, with one burn shared across the lot of them.
localization.TOURS.NarratorsCallSharedWindowContent: This is the same roll dialog the player is looking at. Not a copy — the same roll. What either of you changes, the other sees.
localization.TOURS.NarratorsCallNarratorsHalfTitle: Your half: the move and the Might
localization.TOURS.NarratorsCallNarratorsHalfContent: You judge how the Hero measures up to what they are facing, and which move this is. On a roll you called, these are yours — the player sees them settled and cannot move them.
localization.TOURS.NarratorsCallInvocationsContent:
Invoke the tags of the target, the opposition, or the environment (p.272). Your invocations carry a quill mark and are locked to the roller, so your -2 cannot quietly disappear.

A tag from an actor you have hidden in the sidebar still counts — the player sees its weight as Something unseen, never its name, on the dialog and on the chat card alike.
localization.TOURS.NarratorsCallRollersHalfTitle: Their half: their own tags, and the dice
localization.TOURS.NarratorsCallRollersHalfContent:
The player picks their own tags, trades Power if the move allows it, and presses Roll. The Total updates live for both of you as either side changes anything.

On an Acting Together roll you press it instead — there is no single roller to press it.
localization.TOURS.NarratorsCallPickupContent:
While a roll is open, a click to join strip sits above the player list for everyone not already in it. That is how a helper adds a tag, and how a player who closed the window gets back to it.

There is no chat card to hunt for — the roll posts its own when it lands.
localization.TOURS.NarratorsCallOutroContent:
Call it, set your half, let the player set theirs, and the dice come out.

If your table would rather players reached for the dice themselves, turn on Let Players Start Rolls Themselves in the system settings. Everything in this tour still works either way.
